newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends up vs dollar on light demand.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends up vs dollar on light demand.

text.p: The Indian rupee gained against the dollar on poor demand to end Wednesday at 35.7575/7600 compared to its opening 35.765/775, dealers said.
They said most of the day's trade was between 35.770 and 35.775 per dollar. The rupee traded at a high of 35.7575 and a low of 35.7775 on Wednesday, they said.

"The rupee started to move up right in the morning," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "There was little demand and the rupee gained from opening levels to 35.765. It was stuck here for some time before it started to drift up again in the afternoon."
The rupee moved up against the forward dollar in range-bound trade on good supply of the U.S. currency and light demand, dealers said.
"Most of the day's trade was in a narrow range of one to two paise," said a dealer. "Corporates sold forward dollars and this brought premiums down."
There was some demand for October-delivery dollars, the dealer added.
The annualised premium for six-month dollars ended Wednesday at 3.41 percent against Tuesday's 3.57 percent, dealers said.
